      Food and non-alcoholic beverages represent the largest component of household consumption in Kenya, accounting
                               21                                                 
      for approximately 32.9% of the CPI basket . As an essential and largely non-discretionary category, grocery demand
      is relatively resilient to changes in consumer spending patterns, supporting the defensive characteristics of the sector.
      History of the Grocery Retail Sector in Kenya                               
                                                                                  
      Kenya’s grocery retail sector has undergone meaningful structural evolution over the past decade. The exit or
      retrenchment of certain legacy supermarket operators has accelerated sector consolidation and improved overall
      industry discipline. The market has seen the exit or significant decline of former national champions, alongside the
      emergence of scaled local champions supported by institutional capital. This has created opportunities for stronger
      operators to acquire sites, attract suppliers and expand store networks on more sustainable terms.
                                                                                  
      Supplier ecosystems have also matured, with increased participation by local manufacturers, distributors and
      multinational Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) companies. Improved supplier capabilities, combined with
      greater use of data and category management by retailers, have enhanced assortment planning, pricing transparency
      and promotional effectiveness across the sector.                            
                                                                                  
      Evolution of Kenya’s Retail Market                                          
      The grocery retail sector remains both fragmented, particularly in the informal trade segment, and highly competitive.
      Whilst the distinction between informal and formal retail channels has remained a defining characteristic of the
      market, consumer spending has gradually shifted towards modern trade, creating a significant opportunity for
      organised retailers. The competitive landscape within modern trade has also evolved considerably in the past 10
      years. Modern trade is comprised of three tiers of operators, ranging from large chains with more than 20 stores
      to smaller neighbourhood supermarkets. Most indigenous retailers have operated similar store formats and relied
      predominantly on locally sourced brands, with limited penetration of private label products.

      The historical growth in modern retail between 2000 and 2025 was supported by the growth in the number of modern
      retail outlets, with an average of 40 new stores opened per year over the period. As at end of 2025, approximately
      40% of all modern outlets were located in Nairobi.                          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
       3 Structural Drivers of growth                                             
                                                                                  
      Demographics and Urbanisation                                               
      Kenya’s large and growing population, 54.2 million in 2026, supports a sizeable addressable consumer market for
      grocery retail. Additionally, a growing middle-income consumer segment is increasingly prioritising modern retail
      attributes such as transparent pricing, consistent product availability, food safety standards and broader product
      assortment. Younger consumers, in particular, demonstrate higher adoption of organised retail formats and digital
      engagement, including loyalty programmes, mobile payments and online shopping. These shifts support sustained
      demand for well-located, professionally managed supermarket chains.         
                                                                                  
      The country continues to urbanise at a pace exceeding overall population growth, with 2026 – 2030 projected
      urbanisation rates estimated at approximately 3.4% per annum, versus the average population growth rate 1.9%
      per annum for the same period. At this pace, Kenya’s urban population, currently at 18.5 million, is expected to reach
                                 23                                               
      21.9 million by 2030, and 47 million by 2050 .                              
      Urbanisation drives changes in consumer behaviour by concentrating households in areas with greater access to
      formal retail infrastructure, transport networks and delivery platforms. As consumers move into urban and peri-
      urban areas, shopping preferences tend to shift towards greater convenience (this includes proximity-based retail,
      extended hours and “one stop” outlets), broader product assortment, packaged goods, ready-to-use and ready-to-
      eat products, consistent availability and trusted retail formats. KNBS data indicates that urban households purchase
      98% of their food, and in rural areas the share of food purchased, rather than produced, increased from 30% (2009) to
      78% (2022), indicating the shift towards convenience. These preferences translate to long-term structural changes in
      the retail market. Urban consumers are also exposed to a greater array of modern retail formats, which may support
      increased adoption of modern grocery retail.                                
                                                                                  
      From a retailer perspective, in addition to driving higher footfall at outlets, urbanisation improves the economics of
      store networks, distribution and last-mile fulfilment.                      
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      Urbanisation has been accompanied by the expansion of residential developments across Nairobi and its surrounding
      suburbs, creating new and increasingly dense consumer catchments. This has supported demand for neighbourhood
      retail formats that provide convenient access to groceries and everyday essentials close to residential areas,
      particularly for time-constrained working households seeking convenient and more frequent shopping options
      without travelling to larger destination retail centres.                    
                                                                                  
      The combination of urbanisation, consumer demand for convenience and an increasing number of high-density
      neighbourhoods have driven the industry towards localisation – neighbourhood-led formats such as supermarkets
      and express stores rather than large, destination malls. Kenyan consumers generally have low vehicle ownership,
      are sensitive to transportation costs, face time constraints, limited storage space and prize day to day affordability.
      This has driven a preference towards weekly convenience-driven trips over monthly or occasional bulk purchases.
                                                                                  
      For retailers, neighbourhood formats offer steadier footfall, faster stock turnover and closer competition with informal
      and discount retail, helping protect volumes in a tougher consumer environment.

      Consumer Behaviour and Category Trends                                      
      Consumer behaviour in grocery retail is influenced by price sensitivity, proximity, product availability, freshness,
      assortment and trust.                                                       
                                                                                  
      Kenyan grocery consumers are increasingly value-conscious, with inflationary pressures encouraging shoppers to
                                                                                  
      prioritise affordability and value for money, including lower-priced products, promotions and smaller pack sizes.
      Consumers also make more frequent trips with smaller baskets, supporting demand for convenient neighbourhood
      retail formats.                                                             
                                                                                  
      Changing work patterns and limited time for meal preparation are encouraging demand for convenience. Consumers
      increasingly purchase ready-to-eat and packaged foods and value retailers that provide a variety of brands,
                           24                                                     
      refrigeration and varied pack sizes .                                       
      Private label products are also becoming an increasingly important component of modern grocery retail strategies.
      As consumers place greater emphasis on value, retailers are expanding own-brand ranges to offer quality products at
      more competitive price points than comparable branded alternatives. Beyond enhancing affordability for consumers,
      private label products provide retailers with greater pricing flexibility, stronger category margins and increased
      control over product assortment. They also support customer loyalty by creating differentiated and exclusive product
      offerings, while allowing retailers to leverage scale and supplier relationships to improve sourcing economics. As a
      result, private label penetration is expected to increase as retailers seek to strengthen their value proposition and
      enhance profitability in an increasingly competitive market.                
                                                                                  
      E-commerce, Digital Payments and Omnichannel Retail                         
      Digital adoption is increasingly relevant to Kenya’s retail sector, supported by high mobile connectivity, mobile
      money penetration and expanding broadband access. The Communications Authority of Kenya reported that, as
      of March 2026, mobile subscriptions reached 84.1 million, mobile money subscriptions reached 53.4 million, and
                                       25                                         
      mobile broadband subscriptions reached 62.8 million .                       
                                                              26                  
      The Communications Authority also reported that by March 2026, smartphone penetration had reached 63.7%,
      total mobile data and broadband subscriptions had grown to 62.6 million, and 4G and 5G coverage had expanded
                                     27                                           
      to 97.3% and 30.0% of the population, respectively .                        
      These digital trends support the development of e-commerce, delivery, mobile payment and omnichannel retail
      models. To take advantage of this opportunity, retailers have partnered with third- party logistics providers such
      as Uber Eats, Bolt Food and Glovo for delivery services and have also developed their own in-house platforms and
      capabilities to secure the higher profitability margins associated with e-commerce.
                                                                                  
      For formal grocery retailers, digital channels support incremental customer reach, convenience, loyalty engagement
      and data-driven merchandising. At the same time, grocery e-commerce can require investment in picking, fulfilment,
      last-mile delivery, inventory visibility and customer service, which may affect profitability if order density and basket
      economics are not sufficient. In 2025, e-commerce sales in Kenya contributed USD 0.2 billion (KES 26 billion) to total
      retail expenditure.

       4 Competitive Landscape                                                    
      The Kenyan modern grocery retail market is concentrated among a small number of leading chains that together
      make up 60% of the market, and the remaining market share is fragmented across a long tail of smaller operators.
                                                                                  
      By 2023, six relatively large retailers had exited the Kenyan market, with their assets subsequently acquired by other
                                                                                  
      operators. Two of these were local operators trading under the Nakumatt and Tuskys retail brands, while two were
      foreign-owned operators trading under the Shoprite and Choppies brands.     
                                                                                  
      Prior to their decline, Nakumatt and Tuskys were the largest supermarket operators in Kenya, with peak store counts
      of 65 and 64, respectively. The failure of these local chains has been widely attributed to weak corporate governance,
      overly aggressive expansion strategies and inadequate cost control. In several cases, governance weaknesses
      reportedly extended to poor internal controls, resulting in pilferage and inappropriate supplier relationships that
      undermined financial discipline.                                            
                                                                                  
      Foreign-owned operators faced different structural challenges. These included above-market rental commitments in
      premium locations, with rents charged in foreign currency, which constrained pricing competitiveness and reduced
      footfall, reliance on costly expatriate management with limited local market familiarity, and product assortments
      skewed towards imported goods that were often higher priced and less aligned with local consumer preferences.

      Market Structure and Leading Operators                                      
      Kenya’s modern chain retail base is estimated at c. 500 outlets, spread across approximately 20 retail chains operating
      across key cities and towns. Within modern grocery, market share is concentrated among a small number of scaled
      operators. Sagaci Research estimates that:                                  
                                                                                  
         Naivas is the leading operator with over 31.0% market share;             
                                                                                  
         Quickmart is the second largest operator with around 15.0% market share; and
         Carrefour is the third largest operator with around 14.0% market share.

      Competition includes large domestic supermarket chains, regionally focused operators, discount-led formats,
      convenience stores, wholesalers and emerging online platforms. Competition intensity is highest in Nairobi and its
      surrounding suburban areas, while regional urban centres remain comparatively underserved.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      Competition is primarily driven by:                                         
                                                                                  
         Store location and catchment quality, reflecting the frequent, convenience-led nature of grocery shopping
         and the expansion of residential catchments in Nairobi and other urban centres;
                                                                                  
         Price and value proposition, given high consumer price sensitivity and competition from informal retailers,
         with promotions, pack sizes and private-label products providing key tools to offer value;
                                                                                  
         Assortment, product availability and fresh-food quality, which enable modern retailers to capture a broader
         share of consumers’ grocery baskets and differentiate from smaller informal outlets;
                                                                                  
         Convenience and format, including proximity, parking, trading hours and neighbourhood-oriented store
         formats, which allow modern retailers to compete with the accessibility of informal retail; and
                                                                                  
         Scale and operational execution, including procurement, supply-chain reliability and inventory management,
         which can support competitive pricing, product availability and margins as retailers expand their store networks.

      International operators have historically faced challenges adapting to local consumer behaviour, cost structures
      and real estate dynamics, reinforcing the advantage of local operators with established supplier relationships and
      on-the-ground execution capabilities.                                       
                                                                                  
      Informal retailers remain important competitors because they typically offer proximity, smaller purchase quantities,
                                                                                  
      local consumer relationships and flexible price points. This is particularly relevant in lower-income and residential
      catchments where frequent small-basket shopping is common.                  
                                                                                  
       5 Positioning of Quickmart within the Sector                               
                                                                                  
      Within this context, Quickmart has emerged as one of Kenya’s leading locally founded modern grocery retailers.
      The Company has built a dense network of stores focused on suburban residential catchments, complemented
      by growing exposure to regional urban centres and selective coastal locations. This positioning aligns closely with
      prevailing urbanisation and convenience-led consumption trends.             
                                                                                  
      Quickmart’s model emphasises:                                               
         Proximity-based retail near residential and commuter routes              
                                                                                  
         A strong food and fresh-led proposition                                  
         Competitive promotional pricing supported by supplier partnerships       
         Extended trading hours in selected locations and free customer parking   
                                                                                  
         High customer engagement through loyalty and digital platforms           
                                                                                  
      The Company believes this positioning enables it to compete effectively against both informal trade and organised
      peers. Quickmart’s footprint, customer proposition and operational model are aligned to key structural drivers that
      underpin the growth of modern retail in Kenya.                              
                                                                                  
      As the market continues to formalise, Quickmart’s positioning benefits from:
                                                                                  
         Scale and network effects in procurement, promotions and supply chain execution (in line with the market’s shift
         toward stronger, better-capitalised local champions);                    
         Convenience-led formats and locations that capture high-frequency grocery shopping missions, particularly
         in dense urban neighbourhoods and commuter corridors; and                
         A pathway to omnichannel participation, as online retail expands rapidly from a low base and consumer behaviour
         shifts toward mobile-first discovery and ordering.                       
                                                                                  
      Against this market backdrop, management’s forward-looking plan (including continued store rollout and an
      increased contribution from online) is positioned to capture a share of the growing modern retail market in Kenya
      from:                                                                       
                                                                                  
         the ongoing shift from traditional to modern retail;                     
         the acceleration of digital retail from a low base; and                  
                                                                                  
         the expansion of private label categories within retail.                 
      Within this context, retailers that can leverage scale, maintain pricing discipline, secure favourable supplier
      relationships, ensure inventory availability, manage working capital efficiently and remain relevant across multiple
      customer catchments and channels are better positioned to compete and grow. Quickmart’s competitive position,
      store footprint, operating model and strategy are described in the following “Business Overview and Operations”
      section in this Information Memorandum..

        BUSINESS   OVERVIEW     AND  OPERATIONS                                   
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      1. HISTORY AND OVERVIEW OF THE COMPANY                                      
                                                                                  
      Quick Mart PLC is a supermarket chain operating in Kenya, focused on the retail of everyday consumer goods,
      including food, fresh produce and essential household items. As of 30 June 2026, the Issuer operated a network of
      68 modern grocery retail stores under the “Quickmart” brand across urban and suburban locations across Kenya,
      making it the second largest supermarket chain in Kenya by store count and turnover. Following the opening of four
      additional stores in July and August 2026, the Issuer's network increased to 72 stores.
                                                                                  
      The Company services a broad customer base through a convenience-led retail offering, including value-conscious
      and middle to higher-income households, and seeks to balance competitive pricing with convenience and product
      range.                                                                      
                                                                                  
      The Issuer was formed through the merger of two established supermarket chains in Kenya, Tumaini and Quickmart.
      The Company’s growth trajectory has been shaped by a number of key strategic and operational milestones:
                                                                                  
      Establishment                                                               
      Quickmart traces its origins to 2006, when the late John Kinuthia and his son, Duncan Kinuthia, established the first
      Quickmart store in Nakuru, Kenya. In the same year, Moses Nditika, together with Joram Ngeruro and Elijah Okello,
      founded the Tumaini supermarket chain in Nairobi’s Eastlands area. These two businesses subsequently evolved
      into leading regional retail platforms and later merged to become the foundation of the Quickmart business as it
      exists today.                                                               
                                                                                  
      Independent Development of Quickmart and Tumaini                            
      Quickmart and Tumaini operated as independent, founder-led retail businesses. Each built its own store network
      and customer base within Kenya’s emerging formal grocery retail sector, while developing distinct market positions
      and operating formats in growing neighbourhoods.                            
                                                                                  
      Quickmart’s early growth strategy focused on expansion into suburban and peri-urban catchment areas, supported
                                                                                  
      by an emphasis on convenience, product assortment and accessibility. At the time of Adenia’s investment in 2019,
      Quickmart had expanded its network to ten stores. Tumaini, by contrast, operated primarily in urban areas, targeting
      high-frequency, value-oriented customers through smaller-format outlets in dense neighbourhoods and high-traffic
      locations. When Adenia invested in 2018, Tumaini had developed a network of nine stores concentrated in Nairobi’s
      Eastlands neighbourhood and in the western Kenyan city of Kisumu.           
                                                                                  
      Adenia Partners Investment and Pre-Merger Ownership                         
      The growth of both Quickmart and Tumaini accelerated following investments by Adenia Partners as a private equity
      investor. Adenia held both investments indirectly through its controlling interest in Sokoni Retail Kenya Limited, which
      acquired a 55% majority equity stake in Tumaini in 2018 and a 51% equity interest in Quickmart in 2019, providing
      capital and strategic support to the two established founder-led supermarket businesses.
                                                                                  
      Merger of Quickmart and Tumaini                                             
      In December 2019, Adenia initiated the merger of Quickmart and Tumaini having identified the two businesses
      as complementary in geographic footprint and store format, with limited overlap between their networks. The
      combination offered opportunities to achieve economies of scale across purchasing, category management, supply
      chain, systems, pricing and working capital management.                     
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                         QUICK MART PLC | INITIAL PUBLIC OFFER

=== page 64
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
         62                                                                       
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      The transaction created a unified retail platform by bringing together Quickmart’s suburban and larger-format
      store footprint with Tumaini’s urban, high-frequency store network. The merger also supported the consolidation of
      purchasing processes, operating systems, commercial practices and management structures across the combined
      business.                                                                   
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      From the outset of Adenia’s investment, and continuing through the integration, Adenia supported the
      professionalisation of the Issuer through enhancements to the management team and the introduction of a more
      structured operating, financial and governance framework. Together, these initiatives strengthened the Issuer's
      operational capabilities and established the foundation for its subsequent expansion and development.
                                                                                  
      Transaction Structure and Implementation                                    
      In December 2019, the shareholders of Tumaini and Quickmart entered into a share swap pursuant to which their
      respective ownership interests in the two businesses was combined under a single holding entity, Sokoni Retail Kenya
      Limited. Under this arrangement, the shareholders of Tumaini and Quickmart exchanged their residual shareholdings
      in the operating companies for equity interests of equivalent value in the Selling Shareholder, thereby bringing all
      shareholders of both businesses into common ownership of the combined group.
                                                                                  
      Subsequently, the two businesses were merged via the transfer of Tumaini’s business as a going concern into
      Quickmart, effective 01 January 2020. Following implementation, Sokoni Retail Kenya Limited became the sole
      shareholder of both Tumaini and Quickmart, Tumaini ceased operating as a separate trading business and all stores
      previously operated under the Tumaini brand were rebranded as “Quickmart”.  
                                                                                  
      Key Post-Merger Developments                                                
      Following the merger, Quickmart entered a period of accelerated growth and operational development, driven by
      disciplined store expansion, operational enhancement and the introduction of customer engagement and digital
      initiatives.                                                                
                                                                                  
      The Issuer expanded its store network significantly, adding ten stores in each of 2020, 2021 and 2022, and reaching
      its 50th store milestone in 2022. Quickmart continued its expansion in subsequent years, increasing its network to
      64 stores by 2025 and further to 68 stores as of 30 June 2026. The Issuer opened four new stores in July and August
      2026 increasing its footprint to 72 stores nationwide. This expansion also broadened the Company’s geographic
                                                                                  
      reach beyond its initial core markets, with its presence growing from 5 counties to 16, including entry into Kenya’s
      coastal and eastern regions in 2021 and 2022 respectively.                  
                                                                                  
      In parallel, Quickmart enhanced its customer engagement and digital capabilities. The Company launched its
      Q-Points loyalty platform in 2021 and introduced grocery delivery through third-party partnerships, beginning with
      Glovo in 2023 and subsequently expanding to Uber Eats in 2024 and Bolt in 2025. In 2024, Quickmart also introduced
      QSOKO, its branded online e-commerce platform, as part of its broader development of e-commerce capabilities.
                                                                                  
      Current Positioning                                                         
      Through its expansion and integration strategy, the Issuer has built a scaled national supermarket platform operating
      across Kenya. The Company’s business model is underpinned by:               
                                                                                  
         A multi-format store network serving urban, suburban and regional markets;
         A broad product offering across food, fresh produce and non-food categories;
                                                                                  
         A customer proposition centred on convenience, accessibility and promotion-led value; and
                                                                                  
         Digital and delivery channels that complement its physical store network.

      Through a combination of disciplined organic expansion, operational improvements and digital innovation, Quickmart
      has established itself as one of Kenya's leading supermarket operators. The Company benefits from a seasoned
      management team comprising both long-serving executives and experienced functional leaders recruited to support
      its growth trajectory. This combination has enhanced institutional continuity, strengthened decision-making and
      governance processes, and underpinned the consistent execution of the Company’s strategic objectives.

      3. STORE FORMATS                                                            
      The Issuer operates a network of leased stores across Kenya comprising Hypermarkets, Supermarkets and Express
      stores. This multi-format model enables the Company to adapt its store footprint, product assortment and customer
      proposition to the specific local market characteristics, serving a broad range of shopping missions including
      destination, routine household and convenience-led purchases.               
                                                                                  
      Hypermarkets: Hypermarkets are large-format destination stores located in affluent areas, serving as the primary
      venue for planned family shopping missions. With an average net selling area of 24,601 sq. ft and an assortment of
      approximately 17,000 SKUs, Hypermarkets offer the broadest range of essentials, household goods, textiles, and
      electronics. Customers predominantly access these stores by car, and they are designed to deliver the highest
                                                                                  
      customer spend per visit. As at 30 June 2026, the Issuer operated 26 Hypermarkets, which generated KES 24.9 billion
      of revenue in FY2025, representing 49.5% of the Issuer’s total FY2025 sales. Average basket sizes range between
      KES 1,100 and 1,200.                                                        
                                                                                  
      Supermarkets: Supermarkets are neighbourhood-format stores predominantly situated within residential areas,
      catering to both families and individual shoppers. With an average net selling area of 15,361 sq. ft and an assortment of
      approximately 13,500 SKUs, Supermarkets provide a full range of essentials and regular household items. Customers
      access supermarkets by car or on foot, making them well suited to recurring household grocery missions. As at 30
      June 2026, the Issuer operated 28 supermarkets, which generated KES 20.0 billion of revenue in FY2025, representing
      39.7% of the Issuer’s total FY2025 sales. Average basket sizes range between KES 800 and 900.
                                                                                  
      Express stores: Express stores are compact convenience-oriented outlets located in densely populated urban
      neighbourhoods and high-footfall locations. Designed to support frequent and immediate purchase needs, these
      stores primarily serve urban professionals, younger consumers and single-person households. With an average net
      selling area of approximately 7,638 sq. ft. and an assortment of around 10,000 SKUs, Express stores offer a focused
      selection of essential grocery and convenience products. Customers predominantly access these stores on foot,
      resulting in higher visit frequency. As at 30 June 2026, the Issuer operated 14 Express Stores, which generated KES
      5.5 billion of revenue in FY2025, representing 10.8% of the Issuer’s total FY2025 sales. Average basket sizes range
      between KES 500 and KES 600.                                                
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      QUICK MART PLC | INITIAL PUBLIC OFFER

      The Company's combination of store formats provides flexibility in site selection and enables it to adapt its offering
      to local market conditions while maintaining a consistent customer proposition. The model also supports efficient
      capital deployment and expansion into both established and emerging retail catchments.
                                                                                  
      Leases and Properties                                                       
      The Issuer operates an asset-light business model under which all stores are leased rather than owned. The Issuer
      believes this supports capital efficiency by reducing upfront investment requirements and allowing capital to be
      allocated towards inventory, technology, store fitouts and network expansion. Store leases are entered into on
      standard commercial terms customary in the retail industry and range from 5 to 20 years with periodic rental
      escalation provisions. A portion of the portfolio is leased from related parties on arm's-length terms.
                                                                                  
      The Issuer actively manages its lease portfolio to support operational continuity and minimise the concentration
      of lease expiries in any single year. Management seeks to negotiate favourable lease terms, including appropriate
      lease durations and renewal options, while maintaining strong relationships with landlords. As at 30 June 2026, the
      lease portfolio had an average original lease term of approximately 10.5 years and an average remaining lease term
      of approximately 5.3 years. All lease payments are made in KES. The Issuer has demonstrated a strong track record
      of successfully renewing leases across its store network, supporting stability and continuity of operation.
                                                                                  
      To date, the Issuer has experienced only one store closure, relating to its Shirikisho branch, which occurred upon
      expiry of the lease after the landlord elected to repurpose the premises. The closure was not related to store
                                                                                  
      performance. The Issuer monitors rent as a percentage of sales at each store as a key performance indicator and
      closely reviews locations where occupancy costs are elevated relative to revenue generation. Where appropriate,
      the Issuer implements corrective measures to improve store economics. In addition, the Issuer's established market
      presence, scale and operating track record enhance its ability to negotiate lease renewals and identify alternative
      premises when required.                                                     
                                                                                  
      Store Rollout Process                                                       
      The Issuer has developed a disciplined and repeatable store rollout process that supports its expansion programme.
      New locations are selected following demographic, commercial and competitive assessments, with a focus on
      catchment potential, accessibility, expected sales productivity and strategic fit within the Issuer's network. Proposed
      sites are subject to financial and operational review prior to management and Board approval.
                                                                                  
      Following approval, stores are developed using a standardised fit-out and operational readiness process to support
      consistency across the network. Historically, the Issuer's expansion programme has been funded primarily through
      internally generated cash flows, supplemented by dedicated credit facilities for new store openings. The process
      from site identification to store launch typically takes approximately six months. New Quickmart stores typically break
      even at the EBITDA level from their first month of operation, achieve sales maturity within 12 months on average,
      and deliver a capital payback period of between two and three years.

      The Issuer operates a category-led approach aligned with international grocery retail practices. Under this model,
      each product category is managed as a strategic unit, supporting more disciplined decisions on pricing, assortment,
      promotions, margin optimisation, supplier negotiations and stock availability.
      This approach has strengthened the Issuer’s ability to:                     
         Optimise product assortment at both national and store level;            
                                                                                  
         Align pricing and promotional activity with category performance;        
         Improve supplier negotiations and commercial terms;                      
                                                                                  
         Enhance margin mix across the product portfolio;

      Fresh Category and “Fresh and Easy” Concept                                 
      A central component of the Issuer’s product strategy is its Fresh category, supported by its proprietary “Fresh & Easy”
      concept. Introduced in 2019 and subsequently implemented across the store network, the Fresh & Easy concept
      places fresh produce and related categories at the centre of the in-store customer experience, with approximately
      30.0% of selling space allocated to Fresh offerings.                        
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      The Fresh category is a key component of the Issuer’s customer value proposition and is an important driver of store
      economics. The category supports customer traffic, shopping frequency and customer loyalty, while enhancing
      the overall in-store experience.                                            
                                                                                  
      The Fresh category also contributes positively to the Issuer's margin profile. Margins in the category benefit from the
      value added through in-store preparation activities, including bakery, butchery, deli and hot food offerings, as well
      as the specialised handling, cold-chain infrastructure and operational expertise required to manage fresh products.
      As the category has increased in importance over time, reflecting evolving consumer preferences and demand for
      convenience and fresh food solutions, it has become an increasingly important contributor to the Issuer's mix of
      higher-margin sales and overall profitability.                              
                                                                                  
      Selected Fresh subcategories, particularly fruits and vegetables, are supplied on a consignment basis, reducing
      inventory risk and working capital requirements while supporting efficient cash conversion.
                                                                                  
      Retail Services and Customer Fulfilment                                     
      The Issuer delivers its products through an integrated physical and digital fulfilment model.
                                                                                  
      In-store retailing: The Issuer's physical store network remains its primary sales and distribution channel. The network
      is supported by strategically located stores, extended trading hours, including 31 stores operating on a 24-hour basis
      as at 30 June 2026, and store layouts and merchandising strategies designed to facilitate convenient and efficient
      shopping experiences. These factors enable the Issuer to capture both planned and convenience-led shopping
      missions while maintaining strong accessibility for customers.              
                                                                                  
      Digital and Omnichannel offering: The Issuer has developed an integrated omnichannel retail proposition that
      combines digital ordering with store-based fulfilment, enabling customers to place orders through QSOKO,
                                                                                  
      WhatsApp and third-party delivery partners including Glovo, Uber Eats and Bolt. Orders are fulfilled through the
      Issuer's existing store network, allowing for quick and convenient delivery while leveraging its established retail
      footprint.                                                                  
                                                                                  
      Sales generated through QSOKO and third-party delivery partners collectively accounted for approximately 3% of
      the Issuer's total sales in H1 2026. Since its launch in 2024, QSOKO has experienced rapid growth, with monthly sales
      increasing from approximately KES 0.1 million in August 2024 to KES 19.2 million in December 2025, reflecting growing
      consumer demand for digital shopping solutions and strengthening the Issuer's direct customer engagement
      capabilities.                                                               
                                                                                  
      The Issuer expects digital and delivery-enabled services to form an increasingly important component of its product
      and service offering over the medium term.                                  
                                                                                  
      5. COMPETITION                                                              
                                                                                  
      The Issuer operates within Kenya's grocery retail sector, which comprises both modern organised retailers and a
      large informal retail segment, including kiosks, open-air markets and independent retailers. Despite the continued
      growth of organised retail, a significant proportion of grocery spending remains concentrated within informal
      channels, creating an opportunity for further formalisation of the sector.

      Within the formal retail segment, the Issuer competes with national and regional supermarket operators across urban,
      suburban and regional markets. Competition is primarily based on pricing, product range, store location, convenience,
      customer experience and brand recognition. Competitors vary in scale, format and customer positioning, with some
      focused on value-oriented convenience retailing and others operating larger-format stores with broader product
      assortments.                                                                
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      The Issuer also competes with digital and delivery-enabled platforms that provide customers with alternative
      fulfilment channels, particularly in urban areas. In response, the Issuer has developed an omnichannel offering
      through its QSOKO platform and partnerships with third-party delivery providers.
                                                                                  
      The Issuer believes its competitive position is built on value, reflected in its broad product range, promotion-driven
      pricing and loyalty programme; convenience, reflected in its 24-hour store offering, free customer parking and
      accessible store layouts; and freshness, reflected in its "Fresh & Easy" proposition. However, the Issuer remains
      subject to competitive pressures from existing market participants, new entrants and evolving consumer shopping
      preferences.                                                                
                                                                                  
      6. COMPETITIVE STRENGTHS                                                    
                                                                                  
      The Issuer believes that the following factors may support its ability to successfully execute its business strategy
      and maintain its competitive position within the Kenyan grocery retail sector:
                                                                                  
      Attractive market dynamics: The Issuer operates in Kenya’s large and developing grocery retail market, which
      remains characterised by relatively low penetration of organised modern retail and a significant informal retail
      segment. A substantial proportion of grocery spending continues to occur through traditional channels.
                                                                                  
      The Issuer believes that increasing urbanisation and changing consumer preferences including growing demand
      for convenience, product assortment, value, freshness and digital engagement are supporting the continued
      transition towards organised retail formats. Further, the Issuer believes that modern grocery retailers with scaled
      store networks and established operating capabilities are well positioned to benefit from this trend as consumers
      increasingly migrate towards modern retail channels.                        
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      Differentiated offering and returns profile: The Issuer is one of Kenya's leading supermarket operators, with 68
      stores across 16 counties as of 30 June 2026 and an estimated 15% share of the formal grocery retail market based
      on turnover and store counts as of FY 2025. It has built its position on a customer proposition centred on value and
      convenience. This proposition, delivered through a multi-format store network, allows the Issuer to serve a broad
      cross-section of Kenyan households. The Issuer has been recognised in successive editions of the Financial Times
      ranking of Africa's Fastest Growing Companies, having grown revenue at a CAGR of 18.4% between FY2021 and
      FY2025. Its asset-light model, under which all stores are leased rather than owned, supports a return on average
      capital employed of 47.1% in FY2025.                                        
                                                                                  
      Brand equity and customer loyalty: The Quickmart brand is built around a customer proposition centred on value,
      convenience and freshness. The Issuer offers a broad assortment of grocery and household products supported
      by competitive pricing, supplier-funded promotional activity and strategically located stores. The Issuer believes
      that its established brand, broad customer reach and differentiated value proposition support customer acquisition,
      customer retention and sustainable long-term growth.                        
                                                                                  
      The Issuer has also developed a large and engaged loyalty ecosystem. As of 30 June 2026, the Issuer had
      approximately 2.5 million loyalty members, with loyalty-linked transactions contributing approximately 74% of sales
      during FY2025 and H1 2026. The Issuer believes that this platform strengthens customer engagement, supports
      repeat purchasing behaviour and provides valuable customer insights.

      Scalable and robust operating platform: The Issuer has built its operating platform around four key elements: a
      category-led approach, centralised procurement with a focus on local sourcing, an asset-light, predominantly direct-
      to-store distribution model, under which most suppliers deliver products directly to individual stores eliminating the
      need of a centralised warehouse, and a proven store rollout process. This approach supports product availability,
      pricing consistency and efficient inventory management across the network. The Issuer also maintains a limited
                                                                                  
      warehousing capability for a small number of suppliers and operates its own delivery fleet, enabling the redistribution
      of selected products across stores where appropriate.

      CAGR of 18.4% between FY2021 and FY2025, with like-for-like sales growth averaging 7.1% over the same period.
      For FY2025, the Issuer generated revenue of KES 50.4 billion, adjusted EBITDA (post-IFRS 16 and adjusted for one-
      off and non-recurring costs) of KES 5.4 billion and adjusted profit after tax of KES 1.7 billion.
                                                                                  
      The Issuer's financial performance has been supported by a combination of store expansion, increasing customer
      traffic and growth in basket sizes. Gross margin has improved from 21.1% in FY2021 to 22.5% in H1 2026, supported
      by the Issuer's category-led commercial approach, scale gains in centralised procurement and an improving product
      mix. The Issuer has also benefited from operating leverage and disciplined cost management, which have contributed
      to improving profitability over time. Adjusted EBITDA margin (post-IFRS 16) has increased from 10.1% in FY2021 to
      10.9% in H1 2026, while adjusted net income margin has improved from 1.7% to 3.5% over the same period. The
      Issuer has remained profitable through the specified periods.               
                                                                                  
      The Issuer's business model generates strong operating cash flows supported by favourable working capital cycles.
      The Issuer believes that this cash-generative profile supports the funding of future expansion initiatives while
      maintaining financial flexibility and supporting shareholder returns through dividends, which have grown from KES
      106 million in FY2022 to KES 1.6 billion in FY2025.

      engagement and business transformation. The leadership team has overseen multiple phases of the Issuer's growth,
      including store network expansion, business integration, operational scaling and the development of new customer
      initiatives.                                                                
                                                                                  
      The Issuer's governance framework has evolved alongside the growth and institutionalisation of the Company and
      includes an experienced board, established governance structures, financial and operational controls, and formal

      7. STRATEGY AND FUTURE PLANS                                                
                                                                                  
      Growth Plan (2026 – 2030)                                                   
      The Issuer's medium-term strategy is focused on expanding its store network, increasing customer engagement,
      enhancing operational efficiency and maintaining disciplined capital allocation. The key elements of the Issuer’s
                                                                                  
      strategy are outlined below.                                                
                                                                                  
      New Store Expansion                                                         
      The Issuer intends to expand its store network to 125 stores in Kenya by 2030, with a focus on urban, peri-urban,
      regional and coastal catchments that management believes offer attractive long-term growth potential. Expansion is
      expected to be supported primarily by internally generated cash flows, leveraging the Issuer's asset-light operating
      model, favourable working capital profile and cash-generative business model. The Issuer believes that its track
      record of disciplined execution and established operating platform provides a strong foundation for continued
      expansion.                                                                  
                                                                                  
      To support its growth pipeline, the Issuer has identified 30 prospective locations beyond 2026, of which 13 sites
      are currently under negotiation and 17 sites remain subject to further market research and site assessments. This
      pipeline provides visibility over future expansion opportunities while allowing management to maintain a disciplined
      approach to site selection and capital deployment.                          
                                                                                  
      Maintain Strong Like-for-Like Sales Growth                                  
      The Issuer intends to increase revenue from its existing store network through initiatives designed to enhance
      customer engagement, increase transaction frequency and grow basket size.   
                                                                                  
      The Issuer intends to continue leveraging its Q-Points loyalty programme, customer analytics capabilities and
      category-led merchandising approach to strengthen customer retention and drive repeat purchases. Management
      believes that targeted promotional activity, localised product assortments and the continued development of the
      Issuer's value and freshness proposition will support sustainable like-for-like sales growth across the store network.
                                                                                  
      Improved Digital Capabilities                                               
      The Issuer believes that increasing internet penetration, growing mobile commerce adoption and evolving consumer
                                                                                  
      shopping preferences will support continued adoption of online grocery fulfilment.
                                                                                  
      The Issuer intends to make further investments in QSOKO and its broader digital ecosystem. Beyond providing an
      additional sales channel, QSOKO generates valuable customer and transaction data that supports data-driven
      decision-making across the business. These insights enable the Issuer to analyse customer purchasing behaviour,
      evaluate product performance, optimise category management and implement targeted promotional campaigns.
                                                                                  
      The Issuer expects these capabilities to be further enhanced through the implementation of its new enterprise
      resource planning platform, which is anticipated to provide improved customer analytics, enhanced customer
      relationship management functionality and greater visibility across the business. The Issuer believes that these
      capabilities will strengthen customer engagement, support more personalised marketing initiatives and improve
      the effectiveness of commercial decision-making.                            
                                                                                  
      Over the longer term, the Issuer aims to increase the contribution of digital channels to more than 10% of total
      revenue, supported by rising smartphone penetration, expanding delivery coverage and continued investment in
      digital capabilities. The Issuer believes its omnichannel strategy positions the business to capture evolving consumer
      preferences, extend its reach beyond existing store catchments and support the continued formalisation and digital
      transformation of grocery retail in East Africa.

      8. CUSTOMERS                                                                
                                                                                  
      The Issuer serves a diverse customer base across Kenya, with purchasing needs centred on everyday grocery
      consumption and household essentials. Demand is principally driven by routine, non-discretionary spending, with
      the Issuer’s offering positioned to support frequent, convenience-led shopping missions across its store network.
      As a result, the Issuer benefits from consistent customer traffic and repeat purchasing across different economic
      conditions.                                                                 
                                                                                  
      The Issuer’s customer base spans a broad demographic profile, including value-conscious households, young
      professionals and family shoppers. Its offering is designed to appeal to a range of income segments through
      competitive pricing, convenience and product availability.                  
                                                                                  
      Quickmart has developed strong brand resonance among consumers, particularly female shoppers, supported
      by its value proposition centred on convenience, freshness and affordability. The Issuer's positioning within urban
      and peri-urban catchments also supports high shopping frequency and customer engagement across its network.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      Shopping Behaviour                                                          
      Customer shopping behaviour across the Issuer’s store network is predominantly high-frequency and convenience-
      led, reflecting the essential nature of its product offering. Approximately 68.0% of customers shop at Quickmart on
      a daily or weekly basis, while 54.0% prefer to shop in the evening, consistent with the Company's extended trading
      hours and focus on convenience and accessibility. In H1 2026, the Issuer recorded an average of approximately 5.0
      million customer transactions per month, demonstrating the scale of customer engagement and recurring demand
      across its store network.                                                   
                                                                                  
      Customer Engagement and Retention                                           
      The Issuer promotes customer engagement and retention through Q-Points, its loyalty programme, which supports
      repeat purchases and targeted promotional activity. The programme also enables the Issuer to better understand
      purchasing behaviour and refine its offering in response to evolving customer preferences. In addition, the Issuer
      has expanded customer touchpoints through digital channels, including QSOKO, WhatsApp ordering and third-
      party delivery partnerships, which complement the physical store network and provide customers with additional
      fulfilment options.

      Payment and Transaction Strategy                                            
      The Issuer offers customers a range of payment options, including cash, mobile money and card-based payments.
      Mobile money, primarily M-Pesa, has become an increasingly important payment channel, reflecting broader
      consumer adoption trends in Kenya.                                          
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      M-Pesa accounted for approximately 63.1% of gross sales by value in FY 2025, compared to approximately 44.4%
      in FY21. The increasing adoption of mobile money supports faster transaction processing, reduces cash-handling
      requirements and contributes to operational efficiency at store level.      
                                                                                  
      The Issuer believes that the continued migration towards mobile money payments supports margin protection, as
      mobile money transaction costs are materially lower than card-processing costs while reducing certain security
      and cash management risks.                                                  
                                                                                  
      9. SALES AND PROMOTIONAL  STRATEGIES                                        
                                                                                  
      The Issuer's sales strategy is centred on delivering a compelling customer value proposition through competitive
      pricing, a broad product assortment, convenience and targeted promotional activity.
                                                                                  
      Pricing and Value Proposition                                               
      The Issuer seeks to maintain a competitive pricing position while preserving profitability through disciplined category
      management, supplier collaboration and centralised buying capabilities. Its product offering spans multiple price
      points and is designed to provide customers with value, choice and product availability across key grocery and
      household categories.                                                       
                                                                                  
      Pricing decisions are informed by customer purchasing trends, competitive market dynamics and category
      performance. Management believes that the Issuer's scale, supplier relationships and commercial capabilities
      support competitive pricing while maintaining attractive gross margins.     
                                                                                  
      Promotional Strategy                                                        
      The Issuer operates a structured, year-round promotional programme designed to enhance customer engagement,
      drive store traffic, increase basket values and support category development across its store network. Promotional
                                                                                  
      activities are planned centrally and executed at store level through a combination of supplier-supported campaigns,
      seasonal initiatives, category-specific promotions and localised store activations.
                                                                                  
      Promotional offers are communicated through multiple customer touchpoints, including in-store signage and
      displays, promotional catalogues and leaflets, public address announcements, social media platforms, digital
      marketing channels, SMS campaigns and targeted communications delivered through the Issuer's Q-Points loyalty
      programme. Customer-facing promotional materials are predominantly presented in English and Swahili, reflecting
      the principal languages used across the Issuer's operating regions.         
                                                                                  
      A significant proportion of promotional activity is funded by suppliers through established commercial arrangements,
      including promotional funding, rebates, merchandising support and marketing contributions. As at 30 June 2026,
      supplier-funded promotions support approximately 25% of the Issuer's sales, reflecting the strength of the Issuer's
      supplier relationships and its scale within the Kenyan retail market. The Issuer collaborates closely with suppliers to
      develop and execute campaigns across key product categories, enabling it to deliver attractive value propositions
      while maintaining margin discipline.                                        
                                                                                  
      Promotional activities also support the Issuer's Fresh & Easy brand proposition through product demonstrations,
      sampling and tasting initiatives designed to encourage product trial and enhance customer engagement.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      QUICK MART PLC | INITIAL PUBLIC OFFER
