      1. AUTHORISATIONS FOR THE OFFER                                             
                                                                                  
      The Issuer has obtained all necessary approvals and authorisations in connection with the Offer, including but not
      limited to:                                                                 
      a. approval of the Board of Directors and the sole member of the Issuer in relation to: (i) this Information
         Memorandum so far as it relates to the information of the Issuer as at the date hereof; and (ii) approving the
         listing of and the admission of the Offer Shares to the Main Investment Market Segment of the NSE;
                                                                                  
      b. approval of the Selling Shareholder in relation to inter alia: (i) the sale of the Offer Shares pursuant to the terms
         and conditions of the Offer; and (ii) the establishment of a long term incentive plan, each as more particularly
         described in this Information Memorandum;                                
      c. pursuant to the unanimous written resolutions of the Board of Directors dated 10 August 2026, recommendation
         of the increase in share capital from KES 1,000,000 to KES 50,000,000 and approving the conditional allotment
         of 498,700 Ordinary Shares to the Selling Shareholder;                   
      d. pursuant to the resolutions of the sole shareholder passed on 10 August 2026, approval of the Selling Shareholder
         (being the sole shareholder of the Issuer) in relation to: (i) capitalisation of the sum of KES 49,870,000 standing
         to the credit of the Issuer’s share premium account; and (ii) the allotment and issue of 498,700 fully paid bonus
         shares to the Selling Shareholder                                        
      e. pursuant to the resolutions of the sole shareholder passed on 25 August 2026, approval of the Selling Shareholder
         (being the sole shareholder of the Issuer) in relation to: (i) the conversion of the Issuer from a private limited
         company to a public limited company; (ii) the change of the Issuer’s name from “Quick Mart Limited” to “Quick
         Mart PLC”; and (iii) the adoption of new articles of association;        
                                                                                  
      f. pursuant to the unanimous written resolutions of the Board of Directors of the Company dated 09 September
         2026, recommendation that the sole shareholder approve the subdivision of the nominal value of each Ordinary
         Share from KES 100 to KES 0.20;                                          
      g. pursuant to the special resolutions of the sole shareholder passed on 09 September 2026, approval of the
         subdivision of the nominal value of each Ordinary Share from KES 100 to KES 0.20;
      h. pursuant to the unanimous written resolutions of the Board of Directors of the Company dated 09 September
         2026, (i) recommendation that the sole shareholder approve the increase in the Company’s share capital from
         KES 50,000,000 to KES 800,000,000 by the creation of 3,750,000,000 Ordinary Shares of a par value of KES
         0.20 each, paid up in full at par by the application of KES 750,000,000 from the share premium account, and (ii)
         approval of the conditional allotment of 3,750,000,000 Ordinary Shares to the Selling Shareholder;
      i. pursuant to the written special resolutions of the sole member of the Company dated 09 September 2026,
         approving (i) the further increase in share capital of the Company from KES 50,000,000 to KES 800,000,000
         by the creation of 3,750,000,000 Ordinary Shares of a par value of KES 0.20 each, paid up in full at par by the
         application of KES 750,000,000 from the share premium account, and (ii) subsequent allotment of 3,750,000,000
         Ordinary Shares to the Selling Shareholder;                              
      j. pursuant to the requirements set out in the CM Act and the Regulations, approval of the CMA in respect of the
         Offer and this Information Memorandum, and the listing and admissions of the Offer Shares on the NSE; and
                                                                                  
      k. pursuant to the requirements set out in the NSE Listing Rules, approval of the NSE for the listing and admission
         of the Offer Shares to the Main Investment Market Segment of the NSE.

      2. INCORPORATION  HISTORY                                                   
                                                                                  
      The Issuer was incorporated in the Republic of Kenya under the Companies Act as a private company on 28 April 2006
      under the name “Kids Supermarkets Limited”, and subsequently, pursuant to a special resolution of the shareholders,
      changed its name to “Quick Mart Limited” on 13 January 2008 (being the date of the Certificate of Change of Name
      as issued by the Companies Registry in Kenya).                              
      Pursuant to a resolution of the sole member of the Company passed on 25 August 2026, the Issuer subsequently
      converted into a public company and with effect from 22 September 2026 (being the date of the certificate of
      change of name as issued by the Companies Registry in Kenya), and the Issuer changed its name from “Quick Mart
      Limited” to “Quick Mart PLC”.                                               
                                                                                  
      3. INFORMATION ON  SHARE CAPITAL AND TOTAL ASSETS                           
                                                                                  
      As at the date of this Information Memorandum, the Issuer’s issued and fully paid-up share capital and total assets
      exceed the statutory eligibility thresholds of Kenya Shillings fifty million (KES 50,000,000) and Kenya Shillings one
      billion (KES 1,000,000,000), respectively, as set out below.                
                                                                                  
      Authorised and Issued Share Capital and Capital Reorganisation              
      In August 2026, the Issuer undertook a capital reorganisation to ensure compliance with the eligibility requirements
      for listing on the Main Investment Market Segment of the NSE (the “Capital Reorganisation”).
                                                                                  
      Prior to the Capital Reorganisation, the Issuer’s authorised share capital was Kenya Shillings one million (KES
      1,000,000), divided into ten thousand (10,000) Ordinary Shares of a par value of Kenya Shillings one hundred (KES
      100) each, of which one thousand three hundred (1,300) Ordinary Shares had been issued to the Selling Shareholder
      and eight thousand seven hundred (8,700) Ordinary Shares remained unissued. 
                                                                                  
      The Capital Reorganisation comprised the following steps, undertaken in the sequence set out below:
                                                                                  
      a. an increase in the Issuer’s share capital from Kenya Shillings one million (KES 1,000,000) to Kenya Shillings fifty
         million (KES 50,000,000), together with the issuance and allotment of bonus shares to the Selling Shareholder
         (including, the allotment of shares that were previously not issued) paid up out of the share premium account
         by the application of Kenya Shillings forty nine million (KES 49,000,000) from the share premium account;
      b. a subdivision of the nominal value of each Ordinary Share from Kenya Shillings one hundred (KES 100) to Kenya
         Shillings twenty cents (KES 0.20); and                                   
                                                                                  
      c. a further increase in the Issuer’s share capital from Kenya Shillings fifty million (KES 50,000,000) to Kenya Shillings
         eight hundred million (KES 800,000,000), by the creation and allotment of three billion seven hundred and fifty
         million (3,750,000,000) Ordinary Shares of a par value of Kenya Shillings twenty cents (KES 0.20) each, paid up
         in full at par by the application of Kenya Shillings seven hundred and fifty million (KES 750,000,000) from the
         share premium account.                                                   
                                                                                  
      Following the Capital Reorganisation, and as at the date of this Information Memorandum, the Issuer’s authorised
      share capital is Kenya Shillings eight hundred million (KES 800,000,000), divided into four billion (4,000,000,000)
      Ordinary Shares of a par value of Kenya Shillings twenty cents (KES 0.20) each. The entire authorised share capital
      has been issued and is fully paid up, and there is no unissued share capital. All of the issued Ordinary Shares are held
      by the Selling Shareholder.                                                 
                                                                                  
      Save for the Capital Reorganisation described above, there have been no changes to the share capital of the Issuer in
      the three years prior to the date of this Information Memorandum. All documents relating to the capital reorganisation
      have been made available for inspection.

      4. PRINCIPAL OBJECTS                                                        
                                                                                  
      The Issuer’s principal objective is to operate a scalable and efficient grocery retail platform in Kenya, offering
      accessible, convenient and competitively priced everyday consumer goods, including food, fresh produce and
      essential household items. This objective is supported by a nationwide network of modern grocery stores across
      urban, suburban and selected regional locations, underpinned by centralised procurement, inventory management
      and supply chain capabilities.

      Potential Upstream Shareholder Restructuring                                
      As part of the ordinary course management of its fund structure, Adenia Partners may, following completion of the
      Offer, undertake an internal reorganisation of the Adenia Funds’ shareholding interests in Sokoni Retail Holdings
      Limited (the majority shareholder of the Selling Shareholder), through which the Adenia Funds hold an effective
                                31                                                
      economic interest of approximately 48.6% in the Company. Any such reorganisation may involve the transfer of
      all or part of those interests to an existing fund or to a new fund established and managed by Adenia Partners as a
                                                         32                       
      successor vehicle, which may or may not be managed by the same general partner or have the same underlying
      investors as the Adenia Funds. Any such reorganisation could result in a change in the identity of the fund vehicles
      that indirectly hold an interest in the Company but would not affect the Selling Shareholder’s direct shareholding
      in the Company.                                                             
      Any such reorganisation would occur at the level of Adenia Partners’ upstream fund and holding company structure.
                                                              33                  
      Although this would not involve any direct transfer or disposal of shares in the Company , it would constitute
      an indirect change in the persons holding an ultimate beneficial interest in the Company’s shares. The Selling
      Shareholder’s direct shareholding in the Company and the management and operations of the Company would not
      be affected by any such reorganisation. Public shareholders’ rights would similarly remain unaffected.
      Following any such reorganisation, it is expected that Adenia Partners, through the relevant successor vehicle, would
      continue to manage the Adenia Funds’ interest in the Selling Shareholder through Sokoni Retail Holdings Limited
      and, ultimately, in the Company.                                            
                                                                                  
      Any such reorganisation will be undertaken in compliance with all Applicable Laws and regulations. Adenia Partners
      and/or the relevant Adenia Funds will seek such regulatory approvals or notifications as may be required to implement
      the reorganisation. The Company will comply with its continuing disclosure obligations and will make such public
      announcements as may be required under Applicable Law in respect of any indirect change in beneficial ownership
      resulting from such reorganisation.                                         
                                                                                  
      In addition, following completion of the Offer, the shareholders of the Selling Shareholder may re-arrange (by share
      transfers between themselves, buy-backs or similar reorganisations) their respective shareholdings in the Selling
      Shareholder in such proportions as they may agree between themselves. Any such re-arrangement would similarly
      constitute an indirect change in the ultimate beneficial ownership of the Company.
      31 The Adenia Funds’ indirect economic interest in the Company is derived by multiplying their 95.7% interest in Sokoni Retail Holdings
        Limited by Sokoni Retail Holdings Limited’s 50.8% interest in the Selling Shareholder, resulting in an effective indirect economic interest of
        approximately 48.6% in the Company.                                       
      32 The Adenia Funds are investment funds constituted as limited partnerships. In this type of fund structure, the general partner is the entity
        with legal responsibility for managing the fund and conducting its affairs, while the limited partners are the investors who contribute capital
        to the fund. Accordingly, if the interests of the Adenia Funds are transferred to a successor vehicle that is also constituted as a limited
        partnership, the entity appointed as the general partner of that successor vehicle may either be the same entity that currently acts as general
        partner of the Adenia Funds or a different entity.                        
      33 This means any changes would take place among the private equity funds and holding companies that sit above the Selling Shareholder in
        the ownership chain, rather than at the level of the Company itself.

      Convertible Securities and Warrants                                         
      As at the date of this Information Memorandum, the Issuer has not issued any convertible securities, exchangeable
      securities or securities with warrants attached. The Issuer does not have any shares that do not represent share
      capital, nor does it have any outstanding convertible debt securities, exchangeable debt securities or debt securities
      with warrants.                                                              
                                                                                  
      Long Term Incentive Plan                                                    
      The sole member of the Issuer has approved the establishment of the LTIP for the benefit of eligible employees,
      executives and directors of the Company. The LTIP is intended to serve as a mechanism for talent attraction,
      motivation and long-term retention, with awards subject to performance conditions and vesting schedules set out
      in the LTIP Rules.                                                          
                                                                                  
      Implementation of the LTIP, including the final size of the LTIP share pool as a percentage of the Issuer’s total issued
      share capital, will be subject to the prior approval of the Authority and the shareholders of the Issuer. The Issuer will
      bear all costs associated with the establishment and administration of the LTIP.
                                                                                  
      Reporting in respect of the LTIP will be undertaken in accordance with the Regulations and the applicable disclosure
      requirements, and details of the LTIP will be disclosed in the Issuer’s annual report.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      6. LOCK UP ARRANGEMENT                                                      
      The lock-up period commences on the Listing Date and ends on the date falling 24 (twenty-four) months after the
      Listing Date (the Lock-up Period). During the Lock-up Period, the Selling Shareholder has agreed that it will not,
      without the prior written consent of the Lead Placing Agent, Co-Placing Agent and the Issuer (such consent not to
                                                                                  
      be unreasonably withheld or delayed) and the approval of the CMA, directly or indirectly:
                                                                                  
      a. offer, sell, contract to sell, or otherwise transfer or dispose of any Ordinary Shares or any interest in such number
         of Ordinary Shares legally or beneficially owned by it, representing 60% of the Selling Shareholder’s total
         remaining Ordinary Shares envisaged to be held by it immediately after the Listing Date on the terms set out in
         this Information Memorandum (the "Lock-up Shares" and, the balance of such remaining Ordinary Shares not
         subject to the Lock-up Undertaking, the "Unrestricted Shares");          
                                                                                  
      b. enter into any swap or other transaction or arrangement that transfers, in whole or in part, directly or indirectly,
         any of the economic consequences of ownership of any Lock-up Shares; or  
                                                                                  
      c. publicly announce any intention to do any of the foregoing, in each case whether any such transaction described
         in paragraph (a) or (b) above is to be settled by delivery of Ordinary Shares or such other securities, in cash or
         otherwise.                                                               
                                                                                  
      The Selling Shareholder shall notify the CMA, the Lead Placing Agent and the Co-Placing Agent in writing of any sale or
      other disposal of Unrestricted Shares during the Lock-up Period within 2 (two) business days of such sale or disposal.
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      QUICK MART PLC | INITIAL PUBLIC OFFER

      The lock-up restrictions do not apply to:                                   
                                                                                  
      a. any disposal required by Applicable Law or by an order of a court or competent authority, provided that the
         Selling Shareholder shall give prompt written notice to the Lead Placing Agent and the Co-Placing Agent of any
         such requirement or order, together with a copy of any such order;       
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      b. any transaction undertaken with the prior written consent of the Lead Placing Agent and the Co-Placing Agent;
         and which is approved in writing by the CMA or the NSE as being consistent with the continuing listing obligations
         of the Issuer and the requirements of the applicable Regulations;        
                                                                                  
      c. any transfer (i) by the Selling Shareholder to an affiliate of the Selling Shareholder, (ii) by any shareholder of the
         Selling Shareholder of any shares or other ownership interests held by it in the Selling Shareholder to any fund
         or other entity that is an affiliate of, or under common control with, that shareholder or the Selling Shareholder,
         or (iii) by any fund managed or advised by Adenia Partners (an “Adenia Controlled Fund”) that holds, directly
         or indirectly, an interest in the Selling Shareholder of all or part of its direct or indirect interest in the Selling
         Shareholder to another existing or newly established Adenia Controlled Fund (whether or not managed by the
         same general partner or having the same underlying investors as the transferring Adenia Controlled Fund),
         provided that, in the case of transfers under limbs (i) and (ii) above, the relevant transferee executes and delivers
         to the Lead Placing Agent and the Co-Placing Agent, prior to the transfer, an undertaking on the same terms as
         the Lock-Up Undertaking, and the Selling Shareholder remains liable for any breach of the Lock-Up Undertaking
         by such transferee; or                                                   
                                                                                  
      d. the acceptance of a general offer (whether mandatory or voluntary) made to all holders of Ordinary Shares on
         equal terms in accordance with Applicable Laws and which has been recommended by the Board of Directors
         of the Issuer or has become unconditional in all respects.               
                                                                                  
      Notwithstanding the above, nothing in the lock-up arrangements restricts, prohibits, or shall be construed as
      restricting or prohibiting the Selling Shareholder from creating, granting, or permitting to subsist any pledge, charge,
      mortgage, lien, or other encumbrance over, or otherwise granting security over, any of the Lock-up Shares (or any
      interest therein), or from permitting the enforcement of any such pledge, charge, mortgage, lien, encumbrance, or
      security interest (including any sale, transfer, or disposal of Lock-up Shares pursuant to or in connection with such
                                                                                  
      enforcement).

      14. CLAIMS AND LITIGATION                                                   
                                                                                  
      Due to the nature and scope of the Issuer’s operations, the Issuer is a party to various legal proceedings that arise
      in the normal course of its business, including but not limited to legal proceedings relating to employment, data
      protection, and defamation matters.                                         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      The Issuer has from time to time received routine enquiries and complaints from the Office of the Data Protection
      Commissioner (“ODPC”), as is typical for a retailer of its scale with a customer loyalty programme. Two such
      complaints have been resolved amicably, and a further complaint was dismissed by the ODPC as frivolous. None of
      these matters has resulted in any sanction or penalty.                      
                                                                                  
      The Issuer has retained professional advisors to handle all litigation matters working under the instruction of the
      Issuer’s management, which in turn updates and advises the Board of Directors, on the conduct of these matters
      on a regular basis.                                                         
                                                                                  
      In the opinion of the Directors, the outcome of such proceedings is not expected to give rise to material liabilities
      for the Issuer when considered in the context of the Offer. As at 31 December 2025, the Issuer has made adequate
      provisions in its financial statements in respect of certain material litigation involving the Issuer.
                                                                                  
      Notwithstanding that the legal proceedings to which the Issuer is a party are not considered to be material in the
      context of the Offer, brief details of such proceedings are set out below.

      16. MATERIAL CONTRACTS                                                      
      The Issuer is not party to any material contracts that are outside the ordinary course of its business.
      That said, the Issuer is party to various categories of commercial agreements which are critical for the operations
      of the Issuer’s business and are summarised below.                          
      a. Facility Agreement – The Company is party to a facility agreement with Family Bank PLC dated 18 February 2026
         pursuant to which the Company has access to banking facilities totalling KES 1,850,000,000 (Kenya Shillings one
         billion, eight hundred and fifty million), comprising capital expenditure, secured overdraft, bank guarantee and
         revolving stock loan facilities. The facilities are secured by all asset debentures over the Company’s property and
         assets registered in favour of Family Bank PLC, together with a letter of comfort from the Selling Shareholder.
         Further details of the Issuer’s borrowings are set out in paragraph 11 (Indebtedness) above.
      b. Supplier Agreements – The Issuer has entered into Joint Business Plans and trading terms agreements with
         a number of suppliers for the supply of goods which the Issuer sells through its retail store and online network.
         These agreements are entered into in accordance with the requirements of the Retail Trade Code and generally
         govern the commercial relationship between the Issuer and its suppliers, including payment terms, supply
         arrangements and performance-related incentive structures. The majority of these agreements have a term of
         one year, with a small number having a term of two years.                
      c. E-Commerce Agreements – The Issuer has entered into e-commerce partnership agreements with third-
         party delivery platforms, pursuant to which the Issuer’s products are made available for purchase and delivery
         to customers through such platforms. These arrangements enable the Issuer to extend its retail reach and offer
         convenient delivery options to its customers.                            
                                                                                  
      d. Lease Agreements – The Issuer is party to various lease agreements in respect of its retail store network,
         distribution centres and other operational premises. Further details of the Issuer’s land and leasehold interests
         are set out in paragraph 19 (Land and Leasehold Interests) below.

      17. MERGERS AND  ACQUISITIONS                                               
                                                                                  
      The Issuer has not been a party to any merger, acquisition, division or takeover offer within the five (5) years
      immediately preceding the date of this Information Memorandum.              
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      18. MAJOR CUSTOMERS  AND  SUPPLIERS                                         
                                                                                  
      The Issuer’s business does not depend on a single or small number of major customers or suppliers. Due to the
      nature of its retail grocery business, the Issuer sources products from a diversified base of suppliers across multiple
      product categories and serves a broad consumer base. No single supplier accounts for more than seven per cent
      (7%) of the Issuer’s total purchases in FY 2025 and H1 2026.                
                                                                                  
      The Issuer maintains relationships with multiple suppliers across key product categories and operates a procurement
      function which supports supplier diversification and enables the Issuer to identify and qualify alternative suppliers
      where appropriate. The Issuer has entered into Joint Business Plans and trading terms agreements with its key
      suppliers, which govern the commercial relationship between the Issuer and such suppliers. Further details of these
      arrangements are set out in paragraph 16 (Material Contracts) above. The Issuer also monitors supplier compliance
      with applicable laws and quality standards as part of its supplier management processes.
                                                                                  
      19. LAND AND LEASEHOLD  INTERESTS

      various properties that have been leased by the Issuer are set out in the table below:

      20. PRINCIPAL INVESTMENTS                                                   
      Past Investments                                                            
      Over the last five financial years and during the current financial year, the Issuer’s principal investments have primarily
      comprised the acquisition of property and equipment, store fit-outs and equipment for new and existing stores, and
      investment in technology, digital platforms and supply chain infrastructure in support of its store network.
      Save as otherwise disclosed in this Information Memorandum, the Issuer has not held any material interests, whether
      by way of shares or debt securities, in any other undertakings.             
      Current Principal Investments                                               
      The Issuer’s principal investments currently being made during the current financial year consist primarily of continued
      investment in its store network, including the opening of new stores, store fit-outs and equipment, together with
      continued investment in its technology, digital and supply chain systems.   
      These investments are (i) geographically concentrated within Kenya, being focused on the Issuer’s existing and
      adjacent store catchment areas as part of the continued development of its domestic store network, and (ii) financed
      primarily through internally generated cash flows from the Issuer’s operations, supplemented, as required, by available
      debt facilities.

      be disclosed in due course in accordance with the Issuer’s continuing disclosure obligations.

      23. PLEDGED SHARES                                                          
                                                                                  
      The Offer Shares, together with all other Ordinary Shares in the Company held by the Selling Shareholder, are currently
      subject to a share pledge (the “Share Pledge”) in favour of The Mauritius Commercial Bank Limited (“MCB”) pursuant
      to a share pledge agreement dated 19 December 2025, between the Selling Shareholder, MCB and the Company.
      The Share Pledge was granted to secure certain financing obligations of the Selling Shareholder.
                                                                                  
      MCB has consented to the release of the Share Pledge in connection with the Offer. The Selling Shareholder and
      MCB have entered into a waiver letter and a deed of release dated 30 September 2026 pursuant to which the Share
      Pledge will be released and discharged in full in respect of the Offer Shares.
                                                                                  
      The release of the Share Pledge will become effective prior to the announcement of the Offer results, upon the filing
      of a cancellation notice with the collateral registry established under the Moveable Property Security Rights Act
      (Cap. 499A of the Laws of Kenya). Accordingly, the Offer Shares will be transferred to successful Applicants free
      from any encumbrances arising under the Share Pledge.                       
                                                                                  
      Copies of the waiver letter and the deed of release will be made available for inspection at the locations specified
      in paragraph 26 (Documents Available for Inspection) below, subject to obtaining MCB’s consent on confidentiality.

      International Finance Corporation has conditionally agreed to participate as a cornerstone investor in the Offer. In this
                                                                                  
      regard, IFC has committed to purchase approximately KES 1.94 billion of Offer Shares, representing approximately 13%

      In the event of an oversubscription, IFC's commitment to participate in the Offer will remain approximately 6.45%
      of the Issuer’s outstanding share capital following the Listing and Admission.
                                                                                  
      This commitment is subject to certain conditions, including IFC obtaining all required internal approvals, including
      approval from its board of directors, to purchase up to KES 1.94 billion of Offer Shares at the Offer Price, and to the
      final terms and conditions of the Offer.                                    
                                                                                  
      Save as set out above, any IFC purchase of Offer Shares would be made on the same terms and conditions as all
      other investors in the Offer.

      IFC Policy Agreement Disclosure                                             
      The Issuer will execute a policy agreement with IFC (“the IFC Policy Agreement”) in connection with the Offer. The
      IFC Policy Agreement will contain the key obligations of the Issuer summarised below.
                                                                                  
       1. Environmental and Social Compliance                                     
                                                                                  
         The Issuer will conduct its business in compliance with IFC's sustainability standards and applicable environmental
         and social laws, maintain appropriate systems to identify and manage environmental and social risks, and
         implement any agreed measures required to address identified risks.      
                                                                                  
       2. Integrity, Prohibited Activities and Sanctions                          
         The Issuer will not engage in corruption, fraud or other prohibited misconduct and will cooperate with IFC in
         any related investigation. It will not undertake activities on IFC’s exclusion list of prohibited activities, except
         for ancillary trade in alcoholic beverages and tobacco, which is carved out. It will comply with United Nations
         Security Council sanctions and will not deal with shell banks.           
                                                                                  
       3. Access and Incident Notification                                        
         Subject to applicable law, the Issuer will give IFC and its compliance advisor ombudsman, on reasonable notice,
         access to its sites, records and relevant personnel for compliance purposes. The Issuer will notify IFC within three
         days of any material environmental, social, labour, health, safety or security incident and keep IFC informed of
         its response.                                                            
                                                                                  
       4. Development Impact Reporting                                            
         Within 120 days after each financial year-end, the Issuer will report annually to IFC on development impact
         indicators for its business, subject to applicable disclosure requirements.
                                                                                  
      Sustainability Partnership with IFC                                         
      The Issuer has partnered with IFC to implement a sustainability programme expected to run through mid-2028. The
      programme is focused on three key pillars:                                  
                                                                                  
      Climate Performance and Energy Efficiency: IFC is supporting the Issuer in the development of a greenhouse gas
      ("GHG") inventory aligned with the GHG Protocol, covering Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and the screening of
                                                                                  
      key material Scope 3 emission sources. The programme is expected to establish an emissions baseline, support
      the development of medium- and long-term emissions reduction targets, and enhance alignment with emerging
      climate disclosure standards and best practices. In addition, climate risk assessments of key agricultural sourcing
      regions are expected to be undertaken to strengthen the resilience of the Issuer's supply chain.
                                                                                  
      Responsible Sourcing and Food Safety: IFC intends to support the Issuer in designing and implementing a capacity-
      building programme for smallholder farmers and supplier aggregators, focusing on sustainable agricultural practices,
      post-harvest management and product traceability. The programme also includes the development of a roadmap
      towards ISO 22000/FSSC 22000 food safety certification readiness across the Issuer's supplier network.
                                                                                  
      Food Loss Prevention: With IFC's support, the Issuer plans to establish a baseline measurement framework for food
      loss across its sourcing, handling, storage and retail operations. This will inform the implementation of a structured
      food loss reduction programme aimed at delivering measurable improvements in operational efficiency and
      sustainability performance.

       A limited assurance engagement in accordance with ISAE 3400, does not contemplate testing internal
       controls, assessing control risk or other procedures ordinarily performed during a reasonable assurance
       engagement (e.g., assessing fraud risk; testing company’s records by obtaining sufficient appropriate
       evidence through inspection of source documents, observation or confirmation). A limited assurance
       engagement is substantially less in scope than a reasonable assurance engagement, the objective of which is
       to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the Subject Matter is based on the Criteria, in all material
       aspects, in order to express an opinion. Certain matters may not be identified during a limited assurance
       engagement that may be identified during a reasonable assurance engagement. Accordingly, we will not
       provide a reasonable assurance opinion as part of this Engagement.         
       A limited assurance engagement consists principally of applying analytical procedures, making inquiries of
       persons responsible for the Subject Matter and performing such other procedures as we consider necessary
       in the circumstances.                                                      
                                                                                  
       Our procedures included:                                                   
                                                                                  
       1. Analyse current performance (most recent month within the current financial year, i.e., 2026) and
          compare against the budgeted results for the period                     
                                                                                  
       2. Prepare adjusted Earnings Before Interest, Taxation, Depreciation and Amortization (EBITDA) for the
          last twelve months actual performance (“LTM to most recent month within the current financial year i.e.
          2026”) and compare to current full year budget                          
                                                                                  
       3. Calculate Year to Go (“YTG”) results based on latest full year forecast less YTD results to analyse revenue
          and EBITDA to be achieved in the remainder of current year and compare against:
                                                                                  
          •  The same period in the prior year, and                               
          •  The forecast for the remainder of the year                           
          •  Recent historical events impacting volumes, pricing, mix and costs   
                                                                                  
       4. Discuss the analysis (1-3) with management                              
                                                                                  
       5. Review accuracy of budgeting against actual performance for the last 5 years
                                                                                  
       6. Review the prospective information to be included in the Information Memorandum and report thereon,
          where applicable.

       Conclusion                                                                 
                                                                                  
       Based on the procedures performed and evidence obtained, we are not aware of any material amendments that

                   connection with the Offer) referred to in this opinion were validly issued, remain in full force
                   and effect as at the date of this opinion, and have not been revoked, suspended,
                   terminated, or modified or made subject to any conditions which have not been disclosed
                   to us;                                                         
           3.1.16  given that the Company does not own any freehold or leasehold interest in real property
                   and its entire store network is located in premises leased from third-party landlords, we have
                   not conducted searches at the Kenyan Lands Registry in respect of the underlying title to any
                   leased premises, nor have we independently verified the title of any landlord to the premises
                   demised to the Company. Accordingly, we express no opinion and assume no responsibility
                   with respect to the title of any landlord or any defects, errors, omissions or inconsistencies in
                   the Kenyan Lands Registry; and                                 
                                                                                  
           3.1.17  that the information disclosed by the searches conducted at the Companies Registry, the
                   Collateral Registry and any other public office or registry are accurate and complete, and
                   that such information has not changed since the date of the relevant search.
                                                                                  
           3.2   With respect to matters of fact, we have relied on the representations contained in the
                 Information Memorandum, the Transaction Agreements and the representations of the
                 Company, the Selling Shareholder, and their respective officers and advisers.
           3.3   This opinion is given on the basis of all documents and confirmations provided to us by the
                 Company and the Selling Shareholder in respect of the Company.   
                                                                                  
           3.4   The Transaction Agreements have not been amended or varied, and there are no other
                 arrangements between the parties to the Transaction Agreements which have not been
                 disclosed to us, and which modify or supersede any of the terms of the Transaction Agreements.
                                                                                  
           3.5   There are no facts or circumstances in existence, and no events have occurred, which would
                 by reason of fraud or misrepresentation on the part of any of the parties to them render the
                 Transaction Agreements void or voidable or repudiated or frustrated or capable of rescission.
           3.6   The Transaction Agreements are not void, voidable or unenforceable by reason of:
                                                                                  
           3.6.1   non est factum (that is, circumstances in which one party executes an agreement believing
                   it to be an essentially different agreement and that party was not careless in so doing); or
                                                                                  
           3.6.2   by a party thereto having been induced to enter into it by duress, fraud or misrepresentation
                   or on the basis of a mistake of fact or law.

                    subject to any other material encumbrances.

                    and (iii) the listing and admission of the Company's shares on the NSE.
                                                                                  
           4.1.9.5  The NSE has approved the listing and admission to trading of the Company's shares on
                    the Main Investment Market Segment.                           
                                                                                  
           4.1.9.6  The ordinary shares, when listed on the Main Investment Market Segment of the NSE, will
                    be prescribed as a dematerialised security under the Central Depositories Act.
           4.1.9.7  Save for: (i) stamping of the Transaction Agreements with stamp duty; and (ii) the
                    approvals of the Authority and the NSE referred to in paragraphs 4.1.9.4 and 4.1.9.5
                    above, there are no governmental or regulatory consents, approvals, authorisations or
                    orders, registration, filing or similar formalities required to be carried out in Kenya by the
                    Company in connection with the Offer and the performance by the Company of its
                    obligations under the Transaction Agreements.                 
                                                                                  
           4.1.10  The Offer Shares                                               
                                                                                  
           4.1.10.1 The Offer Shares are existing ordinary shares in the capital of the Company which have
                    been validly issued, are fully paid up, and, prior to being credited to each applicant's
                    central depository securities account, shall be free from all liens, charges and
                    encumbrances                                                  
           4.1.10.2 The Offer Shares rank pari passu in all respects with all other issued ordinary shares in the
                    capital of the Company, including as regards the right to receive dividends and other
                    distributions and the right to attend and vote at general meetings of the Company.
                                                                                  
           4.1.10.3 Upon listing, the Offer Shares will be freely transferable in dematerialised form through the
                    Central Depository and Settlement Corporation Limited and will be held in Central
                    Depository System accounts in accordance with the Central Depositories Act.
                                                                                  
           4.1.10.4 No holder of Offer Shares will be deemed to be resident, domiciled or carrying on business
                    in Kenya by reason only of its holding of such shares.

           5.  QUALIFICATIONS                                                     
           5.1   If any provision of the Information Memorandum or the Transaction Agreements is held to be
                 illegal, invalid or unenforceable by the Kenyan courts, severance of such provision from the
                 remaining provisions of the Information Memorandum or the Transaction Agreements would be
                 subject to the exercise of the discretion of the Kenyan courts.  
                                                                                  
           5.2   The Transaction Agreements must be stamped in accordance with the Stamp Duty Act (Chapter
                 480 of the Laws of Kenya) within thirty (30) days of their execution in order to be admissible in
                 evidence in a Kenyan court. We will attend to stamping within the prescribed period.
                                                                                  
           5.3   Any provision to the effect that certain calculations or certificates will be conclusive and binding
                 will not be effective if such calculations or certificates are fraudulent or erroneous on their face
                 and will not prevent judicial enquiry by the Kenyan courts into the merits of any claim by an
                 aggrieved party.                                                 
           5.4   If any party is vested with any discretion or may determine a matter in its opinion, the Kenyan
                 courts may require that such discretion be exercised reasonably or that such opinion be based
                 on reasonable grounds.                                           
                                                                                  
           5.5   Nothing in this opinion is to be taken as indicating that the remedy of an order for specific
                 performance or the issue of an injunction would be available in a Kenyan court in respect of the
                 obligations arising under any agreement since such remedies are available only at the discretion
                 of the court. Specific performance is not usually granted and an injunction is not usually issued
                 where damages would be an adequate alternative.                  
                                                                                  
           5.6   A Kenyan court may refuse to give effect to a provision to pay the costs of another party in
                 respect of any successful action brought against that party before a Kenyan court and the
                 Kenyan court may not award by way of costs all of the expenditure incurred by a successful
                 litigant in proceedings brought before that court.               
                                                                                  
           5.7   Service of legal process on the Company by post in connection with any proceedings in the
                 Kenyan courts would be effective only if made in accordance with the applicable court rules
                 or with the leave of the court.                                  
           5.8   The opinions expressed herein as to the enforceability of the Transaction Agreements are subject
                 to the qualification that enforcement may be limited by applicable bankruptcy, insolvency,
                 reorganisation, moratorium or other similar laws affecting creditors' rights generally and by
                 general principles of equity (regardless of whether enforcement is sought in equity or at law).
